fields.meta_title: Painting Quote Form That Prices Each Room | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a painting quote form that prices each room, takes photos, sends big exterior jobs to an estimator, and saves every request. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Painting Quote Form Customers Fill Out Room by Room
fields.hero_description: Build a painting quote form that prices each room from your rates and saves every request to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Painter Needs Before Pricing the Job
fields.features_subheading: A painting quote form replaces the walk-through for small jobs. The customer lists rooms, surfaces, and photos, and the price follows.
fields.feature_1:
A price that follows the room list

Set a rate for each kind of room and an add-on for ceilings or trim. As the customer adds rooms, the form totals the quote, and the price shown is the one saved with the request.
fields.feature_2:
Photos attached to the right wall

Give each room or side of the house its own upload field. Peeling trim, water stains, and old wallpaper reach the estimator with the room they belong to, not in a text thread.
fields.feature_3:
Jobs that need a visit go to a person

Write the rule for jobs you will not price online, such as 3 stories or more. Those requests skip the price and go to the estimator you name, by email or in Slack, with the photos.
fields.feature_4:
Counts for doors, drawers, and windows

Cabinet and trim work price by the piece. Ask for the number of doors, drawer fronts, or window frames, set a rate for each, and the quote shows every line with its count and price.
fields.feature_5:
A signature that accepts the quote

Show the customer every line and the total, then a signature box and an accept button. The app saves the signature and the signing date with the accepted quote in a database you own.
fields.feature_6:
The whole app in your GitHub

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository. Run the quote form on your own servers and connect it to the scheduling or accounting tools your crews already use.

fields.tab_content_1:
All 3 rooms and both ceilings, priced at $1,880

Odessa Varnell wants 3 rooms repainted. On the Brushline Painting form she adds 2 bedrooms at $480 each and a living room at $640. She checks the ceiling box in both bedrooms, at $140 each. The form shows $1,880 before she submits, and the request lands in Brushline's table with her address.
fields.tab_content_2:
Any house of 3 stories or more goes to Clemency

Ravelstone Exteriors prices one- and two-story houses online. Any house of 3 stories or more goes to estimator Clemency Wroxley for a site visit. Ezekiel Corwick's house has 3 stories and peeling trim on the north side. He uploads a photo of each of the 4 sides, and Clemency gets an email with all 4 and the address.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each door at $85 and each drawer front at $45

Marisela Pevensey is painting her kitchen cabinets instead of replacing them. Finchwood Cabinet Painting's form prices each door at $85 and each drawer front at $45. Her 22 doors and 9 drawer fronts come to $2,275. She signs on her phone to accept, and the signature is saved with the quote.

Lowell gets each room's color on May 10, 2 days early

Pennbrook Painting offers 24 wall colors, each with a name and a number. Cosima Bartlett picks one for each of her 4 rooms, such as Fog Linen, number 112, for the den. The app saves her picks by room. Crew lead Lowell Ravensby gets the color sheet by email on May 10, 2 days before the May 12 start.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Painting Quote Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a painting quote form that prices rooms from your own rates and hands bigger jobs to an estimator.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down every surface you paint
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put a price on each unit
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Draw the line for a visit
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Choose what the crew lead receives
fields.howto_step_1_des: List each surface your crews price, starting with walls and ceilings. Then add the trim and any cabinet work. Mark the ones you price by the piece instead of by the room, like cabinet doors or window frames. Each surface on the list becomes a choice the customer can add.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Set one rate for each unit on your list: a bedroom, a living room, a ceiling, a cabinet door. Base it on what your last few jobs earned, not on a price sheet. Then total an old job with the new rates and compare it with the invoice you sent.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide which jobs the form will never price, such as houses of 3 stories or more. Those requests skip the total and go to an estimator you name. Ask for a photo of each side of the house so the estimator sees the trim before driving out.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick what reaches the crew lead once a customer accepts: the room list, each wall color with its number, and the start date. Choose a lead time, such as 2 days before the job, and whether the sheet arrives by email or in Slack.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your room rates, piece prices, and site-visit rule into one description. Emergent builds the quote form from it, along with a table for requests and a screen where you read them. When you raise a rate next season, say so in a prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Put a date on every quote
fields.howto_step_6_des: Print a valid-until date under the total, such as 30 days after the request, so an old price does not come back to you months later. Ask for older quotes to show as expired in the table, and send a fresh price when the customer returns.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill the form on a phone the way a customer would, once for 2 bedrooms and once for a 3-story exterior. Check the bedroom total against your own math. Then confirm the exterior request showed no price and reached the estimator with its photos.

faq_plan.q: What is a painting quote form?
faq_plan.a: A painting quote form is the page where a customer describes a paint job and asks for a price. It collects which rooms or exterior sides need paint, along with photos and the address. Simple jobs get a price on the spot, and larger ones go to an estimator.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a painting quote form?
faq_plan.a: Start with your rate for each room type and each add-on, plus the rule for jobs that need a visit. Describe all of it to Emergent's AI form builder in one prompt. It builds the form, totals each quote from your rates, and stores each request in your own database.

faq_plan.q: Should a painting quote form ask what year the house was built?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for any job on an older home. According to the EPA, in general, anyone paid to perform work that disturbs paint in housing and child-occupied facilities built before 1978 must be certified in lead-safe work practices. Make the year a required question, and flag homes built before 1978 so the right crew is assigned.

faq_plan.q: Can one painting quote form handle both interior and exterior jobs?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask first whether the job is inside or outside, then show only that branch. Interiors ask for rooms and ceilings, while exteriors ask for the number of stories and a photo of each side. If you also sell move-out cleaning, keep its rates on a separate cleaning quote form.

faq_plan.q: When should a painting quote form skip the price and book a visit?
faq_plan.a: Skip the price whenever the answers cannot describe the work, such as rotted siding or a ceiling with water damage. Those requests go straight to an estimator with the photos. A standard bedroom repaint, with known walls and a known ceiling, can be priced from your rates.

faq_plan.q: How do I price cabinet painting on a painting quote form?
faq_plan.a: Price it by the piece, with one rate for each cabinet door and one for each drawer front. Ask the customer to count both, and show each count and its price as a separate line above the total. Emergent builds that counter from a sentence in your prompt, and you change either rate the same way.

faq_plan.q: Should a painting quote form ask for photos?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for one photo per room or per side of the house, taken in daylight, plus close-ups of peeling, stains, or cracks. The photos show how much scraping and patching the job needs. For a remodel where paint is one trade among several, a construction quote form fits the job better.

faq_plan.q: How can customers choose paint colors on a painting quote form?
faq_plan.a: Give them a list of your colors, each with its name and number, and one pick per room. Add an option for customers who have not decided, and offer a color visit for them. Save every pick with its room. The crew then paints the den the color the customer chose.

faq_plan.q: How do I follow up on quotes sent from a painting quote form?
faq_plan.a: Give each request a status, such as accepted or declined. Have the app email the customer a reminder 5 days after the quote goes out and alert you at 14 days if nothing changes. Emergent builds the status column and both reminders from a prompt.

faq_plan.q: Can a painting quote form take commercial repaint requests?
faq_plan.a: Yes, with a branch that asks for the square footage, the number of floors, the hours the space is empty, and the bid due date. If a property manager asks you to fill in its rfq form, quote from the same rate table so the two prices agree. Every request lands in a database you own.
